en: The Apadāna of the Elder Girimānanda Pilindavaccha Chapter 7.7 [Verse 1] "Having offered a single lotus flower at the feet of the Buddha Vipassī, I have now attained this state of being an Arhat. [Verse 2] "I was born in a wealthy family, possessing great riches and abundant grain; I was honored by the people, like a moon amidst the stars. [Verse 3] "I had a son named Girimānanda, who was dear to me; I gave him wealth and sent him away to the city of Bandhumatī. [Verse 4] "He went to the city of Bandhumatī, where he saw the Teacher, the Buddha Vipassī; Having seen the Buddha, he paid homage with his head at his feet. [Verse 5] "The Teacher, knowing my mind, taught him the Girimānanda Sutta; Having heard the Dhamma, he took leave of me and returned to his own home. [Verse 6] "I, having heard that my son had become a monk, was filled with longing; I went to the monastery and saw my son, the monk Girimānanda. [Verse 7] "Seeing him, I was overcome with grief and wept; Then, out of compassion for me, he taught the Girimānanda Sutta. [Verse 8] "Having heard the Dhamma, I attained the fruit of Stream-entry; With a joyful heart, I paid homage to my son and departed. [Verse 9] "Having passed away from here, I was reborn in Tusita; There I dwelt for many years, enjoying celestial bliss. [Verse 10] "After passing away from Tusita, I was reborn in the human world; I was born into a wealthy family, possessing great riches and abundant grain. [Verse 11] "I was honored by the people, like a moon amidst the stars; I gave alms to the Saṅgha of monks and maintained the precepts. [Verse 12] "Having practiced the holy life under the dispensation of Kassapa, I have now attained this state of being an Arhat. [Verse 13] "I remember my past lives, extending back through forty aeons; I recall my previous births, as clear as if looking at one's palm. [Verse 14] "I have abandoned birth and death; the holy life has been lived; What was to be done has been done; there is no more of this state of being. [Verse 15] "By the power of that single lotus flower, I have attained this state of being an Arhat. [Verse 16] "I am liberated from all suffering; I have reached the end of existence; I have crossed over the ocean of saṃsāra; I have reached the further shore. [Verse 17] "I pay homage to the Buddha, the Teacher, the Fully Enlightened One; To the Dhamma and the Saṅgha, I pay homage with my head. [Verse 18] "I have attained the supreme peace, the coolness of Nibbāna; I have reached the unconditioned state, free from birth and death. [Verse 19] "I am a field of merit for the world, worthy of offerings and respect; I am a refuge for beings, like a lamp in the darkness. [Verse 20] "May all beings be happy and well; may they be free from fear; May they find peace and happiness, and attain the bliss of Nibbāna. [Verse 21] "This is the Apadāna of the Elder Girimānanda, Recited in the Pilindavaccha Chapter, the seventh."
“My wife has passed away;
my son has gone to the charnel ground;
my mother, father, and brother are dead.”
I dwelt alone in a cemetery.
Tormented by that grief,
I became thin and pale.
My mind was distracted,
and I was tormented by that grief; overcome by the dart of sorrow, I was—
I approached the edge of the forest;
having eaten fallen fruit,
I dwelt at the foot of a tree.
The Fully Enlightened One named Sumedha,
the Victor who brings an end to suffering,
desiring to uplift me—
He came into my presence.
Having heard the sound of the footsteps of the great sage Sumedha, [he approached].
Lifting up my head,
I gazed upon the Great Sage;
when the Great Hero had approached, I looked at him.
Rapture arose within me then,
upon seeing that Leader of the World with my mind one-pointed.
Having regained my mindfulness,
I offered a handful of leaves;
there the Blessed One sat down.
Out of compassion, the Visionary,
the Blessed One, Sumedha, the Leader of the World, sat down there.
The Buddha taught me the Dhamma,
which dispels the dart of sorrow.
Then, uninvited, they arrived.
She has gone from here without permission;
she has gone just as she came—
what cause for lamentation is there in that?
Just as travelers, when the rain is falling,
approach with their goods in hand;
Until the onset of the rains for you;
and once the rains have been completed,
they go wherever they wish.
Thus it was for you with mother and father;
what lamentation can there be in that?
They were but guests and visitors.
Shaken by the wind as it blows—
so too are your mother and father;
what cause for lamentation is there in that?
Just as a snake, having cast off its worn-out skin, goes on its way,
so too [should you leave] your mother and father.
"May he abandon this body here.
Having understood the Buddha’s words,
I cast off the dart of sorrow.
Having generated joy,
I paid homage to the Best of Buddhas.
Having paid homage to that Great Elephant, I—
I worshipped the world-leader Sumedha with a mountain-cluster of flowers that was emitting divine fragrance.
Having worshipped the Fully Awakened One,
placing his joined palms to his head,
he recollected the supreme qualities [of the Buddha].
Having paid homage to the Leader of the World:
“You have crossed over, O Great Hero,
omniscient Leader of the World!”
You uplift all beings through your wisdom, O Great Sage;
you dispel both doubt and perplexity.
You have completely severed [my bonds], O Great Sage;
you have shown me the path through your wisdom, O Seer of Vision.
Arahants who have attained mastery,
possessing the six higher knowledges and great psychic power—
wise ones who travel through the air.
They attend upon him at that time:
the disciples who are practicing, those in training,
and those established in the fruits.
Like lotuses at sunrise,
your disciples blossom;
like the great ocean, you are unshakeable.
Incomparable and difficult to overcome;
thus endowed with wisdom,
O Visionary One, you are immeasurable.
Having paid homage to the Conqueror of the World,
the Visionary One of great renown,
I offer salutations to him while facing the various directions.
I went away in resentment.
But having fallen from the world of the gods,
mindful and clearly comprehending, I have returned.
Wandering through various states of existence from womb to mother’s womb,
having gone forth from the household life—
I went forth into homelessness;
ardent, wise, and meditative,
I made seclusion my domain.
Having exerted himself in striving and having satisfied the Great Sage,
he was like the moon released from thick clouds.
I always wander thus:
devoted to seclusion,
peaceful, and free from acquisitions.
Having fully understood all taints,
I dwell free from taints.
In thirty thousand aeons—
Because I made offerings to the Buddha,
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of offering to the Buddha.
The defilements have been incinerated by me;
all states of existence have been uprooted;
all taints are completely exhausted.
Now there is no further becoming.
Welcome indeed has come to me... [as before] ...
Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken:
the four analytical knowledges... [and so forth].
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, indeed, the Venerable Elder Girimānanda spoke these verses.
This is the seventh legend of the Elder Girimānanda.
